titles.521: Man. Post. Cap. IX: PLAC — first sense: immanent act in God's mind
titles.522: Man. Post. Cap. IX: PLAC — second sense: where/when is the declaration?
titles.523: Man. Post. Cap. IX: PLAC — third sense: penalty enters, not sin; two entries
titles.524: Man. Post. Cap. IX: PLAC — 'entered' fits hereditary properly, actual only remotely

latin.521: Si primum eligis, actio est Dei immanens: non enim alibi est aut esse potest quam in Deo, in Dei mente. Vocant quidem nonnulli Theologi actiones divinae mentis & voluntatis, actiones ad extra, quia habent pro obiecto creaturas: at non eas ideo faciunt minus immanentes, ut facit hoc loco vir doctus, <PRIVATE_ADDRESS> inconsiderate.
latin.522: Si secundum, ubi & quando facta est illa declaratio, & num extra nos, an intra nos?
latin.523: Si tertium, repugnat Apostolus qui peccatum hoc loco distinguit a poena peccati quam mortem vocat. Inflictione poenae, hoc est, mortis, intrat quidem mors seu poena, sed non intrat peccatum. Alius est in verbis Apostoli introitus peccati, alius introitus mortis, ille causa est huius.
latin.524: Deinde, si peccatum actuale Adami non intravit in mundum, nisi ratione corruptionis haereditariae, fatendum est hoc attributum intrasse in mundum, seu homines, convenire per se & proprie & proxime corruptioni haereditariae, remote tantum, & illius corruptionis ratione, peccato actuali Adami. Si igitur corruptio illa est vere & proprie peccatum, etiam post baptismum, ut nostri adversus Pontificios tuentur, nonne manifestum est, peccatum quod in mundum intravit, eius potius descriptionem esse quam peccati actualis Adami?
latin.525: Huc accedit quod Apostolus ait per hoc peccatum mortem introiisse in mundum. Introitus in mundum commune est peccati & mortis attributum. Utrumque in mundum introiit, sed peccatum per se, mors per peccatum. Mors autem introiit reapse, non imputatione, & mors quae introiit in mundum non est mors unius Adami, sed totuplex quot sunt homines. Cum ergo constet esse peccatum, nempe corruptionem haereditariam, quod eodem prorsus modo introierit in mundum, quid est, cur id hoc loco non intelligamus potius, quam id quod neque introitu in mundum, neque numero morti correspondeat?
latin.526: Denique si per peccatum quod in mundum introiit, peccatum actuale Adami intelligitur, necesse est, ut Apostolus, vel prorsus omiserit corruptionem inhaerentem, vel eam mortis nomine comprehenderit. Hoc utrumque est falsum; Ergo & illud.

pass_a.521: Pick the first, and imputation is God's own inward act: nowhere but in God, in God's mind. Some call mind-and-will acts 'toward the outside' because creatures are their object—yet they stay immanent. The learned man here makes them less so, rather inconsiderately.
pass_a.522: If the second sense: name the place and the hour of that external sentence—and say whether it landed outside us or inside us.
pass_a.523: If the third, the Apostle fights you: here he distinguishes sin from sin's penalty, which he calls death. By infliction of penalty—that is, of death—death or penalty does enter, but sin does not. In his words sin's entry is one thing, death's another; the former is cause of the latter.
pass_a.524: Next: if Adam's actual entered the world only by reason of hereditary corruption, then this attribute 'entered into the world / into humans' fits hereditary corruption of itself, properly, and nearest—and Adam's actual only remotely, and for that corruption's sake. So if that corruption is truly and properly sin even after baptism, as ours hold against the Papists, is it not plain that the sin which entered the world is its description rather than Adam's actual?
pass_a.525: Add that Paul says through this sin death entered the world. Entry into the world is common to sin and death: both entered, but sin of itself, death through sin. Death entered in very deed, not by imputation; and the death that entered is not Adam's one death but as many as there are humans. Since there is a sin—hereditary corruption—that entered in exactly the same way, why not take that here rather than what matches death neither in world-entry nor in number?
pass_a.526: Finally: if the sin that entered means Adam's actual, Paul must either have wholly omitted inhering corruption or have packed it under the name of death. Both are false; therefore so is that. Tip before working the two falsehoods.

521: If you choose the first, it is an immanent action of God: for it is not elsewhere, nor can it be, than in God, in God's mind. Some theologians indeed call the actions of the divine mind and will actions toward the outside, because they have creatures for their object: but they do not therefore make them less immanent, as the learned man does in this place, rather inconsiderately.
522: If the second, where and when was that declaration made, and is it outside us, or inside us? The learned man does not say.
523: If the third, the Apostle conflicts, who in this place distinguishes sin from the penalty of sin which he calls death. By the infliction of penalty, that is, of death, death or penalty indeed enters, but sin does not enter. One thing in the Apostle's words is the entry of sin, another the entry of death; that is the cause of this.
524: Next, if Adam's actual sin did not enter into the world except by reason of hereditary corruption, it must be confessed that this attribute of having entered into the world, or into humans, agrees of itself and properly and nearest with hereditary corruption, only remotely, and by reason of that corruption, with Adam's actual sin. If therefore that corruption is truly and properly sin, even after baptism, as ours hold against the Papists, is it not manifest that the sin which entered into the world is rather its description than that of Adam's actual sin?
525: To this is added that the Apostle says that through this sin death entered into the world. Entry into the world is a common attribute of sin and of death. Both entered into the world, but sin of itself, death through sin. But death entered in very deed, not by imputation, and the death which entered into the world is not the death of one Adam, but as manyfold as there are humans. Since therefore it is agreed there is a sin, namely hereditary corruption, which entered into the world in exactly the same way, what is there why we should not understand that in this place rather than that which corresponds to death neither by entry into the world, nor by number?
526: Finally if by the sin which entered into the world Adam's actual sin is understood, it is necessary that the Apostle either wholly omitted inhering corruption, or comprehended it under the name of death. Both of these are false; Therefore that also.
